newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan EVA buying planes from Boeing, McDonnell.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan EVA buying planes from Boeing, McDonnell.

text.p: Taiwan's EVA Airways, a unit of shipping giant Evergreen Marine, said on Monday that an imminent purchase of passenger planes would be sourced from both Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.
EVA spokesman Nieh Kuo-wei declined to give details on the number of aircraft being purchased, the value of the deals or when they would be signed and announced.
He confirmed, however, that the purchase would involve planes from both Boeing and McDonnell Douglas, who announced plans on Sunday to merge under the Boeing name.
"We do have plans to buy planes from both Boeing and McDonnell Douglas, but I cannot give details now," Nieh said.
Nieh again declined to comment on a report in Taiwan's Econonic Daily News last Thursday that said the plane purchase deal was worth more than US$1 billion.

Speculation about EVA purchases was triggered a week ago when General Electric Co announced its engine unit had won a US$750 million order from EVA for 82 GE CF6-80 turbofan engines -- suitable for Boeing or McDonnell Douglas planes.
The Economic Daily News quoted unnamed sources as saying the GE announcement indicated EVA soon would unveil a plan to buy at least six mid- and long-haul passenger and cargo planes.
The sources did not say which planemaker would be selected.
EVA said in May it was considering buying 10 or more Boeing 747-500 passenger planes, worth some US$200 million each.

EVA now owns 28 planes -- 12 Boeing 747-400s for long-haul international routes, five Boeing 767-300s, four Boeing 767-200s, six McDonnell Douglas MD-11s and one newly delivered MD-90. EVA took deliver in October of the first of six MD-90 planes bought from McDonnell Douglas in 1995.
The carrier, Taiwan's second international airline, made a net profit of T$198 million in 1995 after four years of losses since it began operations in 1991.
In 1995, EVA made a net profit of T$198 million on sales of T$28.86 billion, compared with a loss of T$950 million in 1994 on sales of T$19 billion, Nieh said.
For 1996, EVA has set a net profit target of some T$600 million on sales of T$35 billion, Nieh said.
EVA has forecast three straight years of profits and plans to listed in the local stock market in 1998, he said.
U.S. aircraft titans Boeing and McDonnell Douglas said in Washington on Sunday they would merge to create the world's largest aerospace company in a deal worth about $13.3 billion.
The combined firm, to be based at Boeing headquarters in Seattle and to operate under the Boeing Co name, was projected to have 1997 sales of about $48 billion, up from about $35 billion in 1996.
